title: The FCA keeps firms accountable for their AI agents
summary: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority published a standing page on its approach to agentic AI. It sets no new rules, but firms keep full accountability under the Consumer Duty and the Senior Managers regime when agents act for them. Firms must decide how they verify an agent, what consent covers, and whether to accept payments instructed by an agent.
whyItMatters: Liability for agent actions stays with the regulated firm, so verification becomes a bank's problem rather than the regulator's.
